architectReview.evidence: G004 is implemented as a backend-owned, client-neutral photo diary core contract usable by both web and mobile clients: direct single-image upload, EXIF metadata extraction, manual GPS/location correction, folder-member visibility, title/body/place/tag editing, CRUD, filtered list, detail, and map projection endpoints. The implementation preserves the approved folder-type separation by allowing diary entries only in PHOTO_DIARY folders and routes all diary writes through FolderCapabilityPolicy.

executorQa.evidence: The full Spring Boot verification suite and OpenAPI refresh pipeline pass. New diary API tests exercise upload, metadata dimensions, manual location fallback when EXIF GPS is missing, create/list/filter/map/detail/update/delete, folder type isolation, viewer read/write role behavior, and invalid upload rejection.

contractCoverage.obligation: Authenticated clients can upload exactly one supported image and receive a persisted media asset with dimensions and EXIF metadata fields.
Diary creation can use EXIF GPS when present and requires explicit latitude/longitude correction when GPS is unavailable; saved coordinates can be corrected on update.
Photo diary entries support title, body, place name, captured time, and normalized tag editing.
Folder members can read list/detail/map views, and authorized writers can create, update, and delete diary entries.
Photo diary entries cannot be created in REELS_PLACE folders, preserving photo_diary and reels_place separation.
The backend-owned OpenAPI contract exposes the same bearer-secured photo diary behavior to both web and mobile clients rather than creating platform-specific divergent flows.

adversarialCases.scenario: A client attempts to direct-upload a text file as media.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The request is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

adversarialCases.scenario: A valid image has no EXIF GPS and the diary create request omits latitude/longitude.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The request is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT until the user manually supplies a location.

adversarialCases.scenario: A diary entry is created in a REELS_PLACE folder.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The request is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

adversarialCases.scenario: A viewer reads a diary entry and then attempts to update it.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The read succeeds and the write is denied with FOLDER_WRITE_NOT_ALLOWED.

adversarialCases.scenario: A diary create request sends duplicate tags that differ only by case or whitespace.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The entry is persisted with normalized unique tags.

adversarialCases.scenario: Runtime OpenAPI is compared with the checked-in contract after adding diary and media endpoints.
adversarialCases.expectedBehavior: The checked-in contract matches runtime docs and exposes bearer-protected diary/media operations for both client types.

iteration.evidence: After implementing the media and diary core, the focused diary API suite and the full OpenAPI refresh plus Spring Boot test suite were rerun cleanly against the current repository state.
